text: The only exception to importation into Singapore for non-compliant packages will be for the purposes of re-exporting out of Singapore without coming into the Singapore market.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked if we regulate the size of the cigarettes themselves, presumably because with the standardised packaging measures in place, one could foreseeably see tobacco companies distinguishing themselves by having different cigarette sizes or lengths.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Dennis Tan might wish to note that under the new section 17(3)(a) which is found in clause 3 of the proposed Bill, we already provide for the ability to regulate not just the packaging, but also the size of the actual tobacco product or cigarette itself.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh has asked if MOH would consider restricting nicotine and other harmful substances in tobacco products.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This is again not quite the emphasis of the Bill here.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But I would like to inform the House that under the Act currently, there are already limits set for tar and nicotine in cigarettes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We note that the US Food and Drug Administration is studying the possibility to lower the nicotine content of cigarettes to non-addictive levels.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There will be public health benefit if cigarettes can be made to be non-addictive but, of course, quitting smoking would be much easier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked if MOH would consider requiring broadcast media to carry reminders of the harmful effects of tobacco in all screenings of videos, movies or drama productions, where the scenes of smoking cannot be edited and cut.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There are presently already content guidelines for media broadcasters to exercise due diligence in the depiction of smoking on television (TV), in movies and other media channels.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But as Prof Lim Sun Sun did point out, today, the media is more than just traditional television, videos or movies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: There is also social media on the Internet.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: With that in mind, we look at the different suite of measures and work out what is best to address and arrest these images.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In broad terms, broadcasters must avoid conveying the impression in programmes that smoking is socially acceptable, glamourous or harmless.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, portrayal of smoking in films continues to be a problem worldwide and cannot at present be completely eradicated.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: However, we will study the suggestion to display anti-smoking messages or advertisements before any films containing tobacco imagery are shown.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if we could consider restrictions on certain brand variant names.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will give it consideration but, as Mr Louis Ng knows, we prescribe the way in which the name of the brand as well as the variant are presented in terms of style, font and colour on the package.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will look at the names to ensure that they are not misleading, which is already the current requirement.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have given very careful, due and deliberate consideration to the available primary evidence, consulted with experts in different fields and different types of experts and sought the public’s views multiple times.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We acknowledge the impact that the introduction of the SP Proposal will have on tobacco and its related industries, potentially in terms of costs and other ways, as highlighted by various Members, including Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, and we have taken and will continue to take steps to mitigate this impact.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These objectives and outcomes warrant its introduction in Singapore as an additional measure in our comprehensive, multi-pronged, multifaceted tobacco control strategy.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: I hope I have sufficiently addressed Members’ concerns and am grateful for the support that has been shown for the SP Proposal received from members of the public and also from this House.
